[quote=montfleur;61607793][b]June 13, 2028: The National Assembly[/b]

The King of Montfleur, having been made aware of the growing matter in their southern neighbour, Rosenmarkke, would seek to bring the matter to the National Assembly, convening an extraordinary session of the assembly and the senate, and he made his case for the matter.

My friends and fellow strivers of this our government,

Regarding the disturbances that have begun to occur to the south of our nation, it is not right for Montfleur to get involved.

Jeers from the nationalists roared from one side of the chamber as the king paused. 

However, continued the king, Should the people of Rosenmarkke call upon our aide, I ask you, is it not right to help them?

He paused again as jeers filled the hall from the left coalition this time.

My friends, neutrality has done Montfleur a bad way, it has left her far behind her peers, and has shown to be ineffective in the preservation of this state, I ask you, should our friends and allies in Rosenmarkke call for our help, will we not help them?

More jeers from the left, the king leaned on his right and pointed at them from the podium.

The era of Les Optimistes, it is over, for too long the ideals of peace and harmony have threatened our very state, should the topic of merging with Rosenmarkke come forward, I say we vote yes! Yes! Yes! declared Henri, pounding the podium. 

The assembly hall filled with the roar of yess and nos and jeers as the deputies of the chamber forced their way into the throng of legislators who had left their seats and now filled the aisles of the chamber, shouting slogans for or against the motion. 

I say we vote yes! And more than this, I say we begin to move towards facilitating the union! Through the formation of a congress of constitution! declared Henri, shouting over the roar. 

At this point, Eleonore had begun to bang the gavel on the podium to demand order; however, the king's words had incensed the legislators greatly as those in the communist party ripped off their wigs and stomped on them, while the moderates were jostled about by their peers, and the nationalist factions were cheering and shouting. 

My dear friends, continued the king over the roar, The process will be long, and it will be hard, but we must consider the possibilities that may come in the following months, should the discontent in Rosenmarkke among its citizens rise to the point where the government is unable to sustain itself, and the regions and estates of Rosenmarkke begin passing resolutions to secede from Rosenmarkke to join Montfleur, which is a possibility, we must be ready,

The roar continued as guards moved to the sides of the podium, attempting to usher the king out. We will win! Montfleur always wins! declared Henri, lifting his cane and waving it as the guards pushed him out the back door of the chamber. 

[nation]New Westmore[/nation]
[nation]Qianxun[/nation]
[nation]Vespurias[/nation]
[nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation][/quote]

Within an hour of returning to the palace, the news media, the social media, and the general public had leapt quickly to react to what was deemed as an unusual outburst. 

It had taken thirty minutes for the chamber to be cleared, with the heads of the individual parties reacting to the kings speech.

Irrational madness, to undo or even suggest undoing over 100 years worth of diplomacy on the first notion of Rosenmarkke having some internal issues after a war, the Jean Baptiste party will not stand for this, and will be seeking a motion to censure the king from speaking in the assembly for a time, said Jean Luc Rousmonde the newly elected head of the Montfleurois socialist party.

While the king of Montfleur has his right to say his opinion, we do not stand for disorder in this country, the Montfleurois Democratic Union will be seeking a motion of censure, quoted Llilan Lucard, head of the MDU.

The public and media noted the odd silence from the right, with many surprised that not even the moderate Blue Union party had been silent.

Henri, now in his study sat behind his chair with the television news running, he smiled at Eleonore who had just gotten off the phone with several members of the Senate.

Well Eleonore, we succeeded, the people will now look into the Rosenmarkket situation, grinned Henri.

Eleonore gave him an exasperated look, At the expense of days worth of backpeddling, she replied with a sigh.

The king picked up a red stress ball and threw it at her to catch,  Look, the political situation in Rosenmarkke is degraded, the Haakon fellow, Haakon the Hack, is merely a puppet of the council of 99they have yet to reassemble the SCSIDthe reunion is inevitable, 

And what if it isnt? Asked Eleonore, throwing the ball back.

Then we break neutrality, simple, replied Henri, throwing it back at her.

You want us to invade a THEP state? She scoffed, Thats absurd!

Look, the regime that controls Rosenmarkke is bound to draw us into a war anyways, we must cut the head off the snake, replied Henri.

This is madness. At this point, we might also join the socialist international and rename your title to Citizen 1, replied Eleonore, throwing the ball back at him.

We might, winked Henri, catching it and placing it back on the desk.

Eleonore rolled her eyes, If you werent placed upon the throne by the grace of God and the pope, I would have you removed so quickly by a vote. 

See, this is why I picked you to be the president of the government, aside from the fact that I dated you back in the old days, joked Henri.

Oh, please, lets not go there, replied Eleonore, I broke up with you because you were insufferable, and I only accepted this position, because you still are insufferable.

Henri shrugged, Fine with me. 

Anyways, replied Eleonore with a shake of her head, What are we going to do? Lets be real here for a moment, Rosenmarkke is not collapsing to some guys in wigs with canes, 

Right-o, replied Henri.

Montfleur is not just going to support suddenly absorbing Rosenmarkke after 200 years, she continued.

Correct again, replied Henri.

So, what? 

Well, Ellie, began Henri.

Please dont call me that, interjected Eleonore.

Henri shrugged, Alright, Eleonore, here is what I see, madame duchesse, the duc of the islands that once were the merchant republic has openly broken with the Rosenmarkket government, I expect him to actively join ranks with these wigged fellows with the canes, now the duc is a popular person, as are most of the regional leaders. 

Sowe just need to push them to move for secession? asked Eleonore.

Bingo, and what better way to do that but to openly support the movement, eh?

You saw how the parties reacted today, replied Eleonore.

Henri shrugged, withdrawing from his desk a Vicodin pill bottle and popping one in his mouth, Theyll figure it out, at worst, we slam their head into a car door over and over again in the next election and watch as they bleed members, its a bad look if they are seen supporting a tyrannical security state,

Alright, well, theres a press briefing later today. I assume you will be giving some clarifying remarks? asked Eleonore, moving to the door.

Well see, I am not one to mince words, duchesse, smiled Henri.

[quote=qianxun;61561837][spoiler=[b]The Issue with Bravery[/b]][b]The Issue with Bravery[/b]

"Adventurism has never created anything good." Cui Fang bemoaned, sighing deeply as he crumpled into his chair. It's been a few minutes since news reached him of the social impact of Technate interference in Dhornaper. "I told people that adventurism destroys the people's movements. But did those technocrats listen?"

"It's an awful situation, Comrade Cui." Argo Lo Pilato responded, his eyes glued to his phone, which he had been swiping away at since the crackdown began.

"More than awful, Comrade Lo Pilato. We've just watched yet another revolution be destroyed because it couldn't resist the temptation of being seen. See now? This is why I constantly criticize people for trying to find some common ground among the political Left. We alone are the Left! Everything else is constituted by fundamental misunderstandings of the people's revolution, misunderstandings that lead to abominations like this!"

"Well..."

"Well what?!"

Argo Lo Pilato stood back a moment to recompose himself. When Chairman Cui was angry, it was the sort of anger that would instigate blood vendettas or wars in distant lands. After choosing his words carefully, Lo Pilato carefully put down his phone and dragged a stool over near to Cui, then sitting down upon it. He leaned in, his expression calm but cautious, and he began to speak low and quietly, "Many heroes have been sacrificed today, Comrade Cui, but the spirit of the people's movement still exists among the Dhora, if you'd be willing to help me out here."

"Help you out?" Cui responded, one eyebrow raised high.

"The Astanirans have been observing the situation very closely, Comrade." Lo Pilato continued, "The communist movement still exists in Dhornaper, but it's currently scrambling to survive. We've received reports of one particularly vigorous youth who somehow swam some 35 kilometers to reach one of the Astaniran boats that had been shadowing the Dhora area of responsibility."

"Is he alive?"

"She, comrade. It was a girl. She swam after her brother was shot. Now we have her safe and sound, but only barely. I'm asking for your help now because I believe, no, this entire International believes that more of our fellow comrades can yet be saved so long as we track the Dhora waters, international flights, perhaps even those that opted to take their chances by taking the long way north."

"... You do understand that you're suggesting that we create yet another hostile power against us, right comrade? And so soon after we've elected to involve ourselves in the crisis at Rosenmarkke..."

"I understand it completely." Lo Pilato replied, his voice fully assured. "God is probably a strange concept to you Qianxun folk, Comrade Cui, but it's something important to us Sanguinians. We believe that God is a most wonderful power who directs us to do what must be done for the sake of the human race. This mission is why we practice socialism, and is why I believe that even to save just one more life is absolutely pertinent to the people's revolution."

"I'm not here to judge your believes, comrade." Cui said, rubbing his temples as he stood up from his seat. "So, if you really believe in this mission of yours, then go ahead. I won't oppose you. If you need, for whatever reason, any Qianxun assets in Astanir, contact Yun Caibo. As you can see, I'm rather tired at the moment, so..."

"Yes, yes, that's fine. You just rest there, comrade. Write a new polemic if you want, I'll make sure that my personal endeavors don't trouble a deep mind."

"Oh piss off." Cui exclaimed, waving Lo Pilato off as he quickly shuffled out of the office door. "... Hah... [i]attendre et espérer[/i]..."[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Operation Misericordia[/b]][b]Operation Misericordia[/b]

What remains of Dhora communism has been crushed underfoot by the brutality of monarcho-fascism. While the Socintern continues to hold true to the axiom that a movement cannot simply be destroyed through the destruction of its adherents, this does not mean that sympathetic forces will simply let their fellow brethren be butchered before their very eyes.

Days before, ad hoc rescue operations had already been underway off the coast of Dhornaper, with Astaniran ships and boats lining up to rescue any fleeing Dhora able to find safety aboard their craft. However, this method has led to hefty casualties among fleeing communists, most of whom would either be torn apart piecemeal by the Dhora coast guard, or else simply drown from a lack of skill or stamina in the depths before reaching their ships.

Now therefore, Horano Benir, the current president of the People's Republic of Astanir, has accepted the finalized version of a massive smuggling operation to protect the remnants of Dhornaper's communist movement from total obliteration. With extensive material support from SummitONE Solutions, the Qianxun Socialist Ethics Commission, and individual backers in the Sanguinian Social Renaissance Party, the Astaniran Democracy Navy would launch Operation Misericordia, a massive repatriation campaign to save any fleeing Dhora attempting to escape either by sea from the south or by land from the north.

In the south, Astaniran replenishment ships and boats would be sent to hover just beyond the Dhora area of responsibility, with specialized equipment such as covert submersibles to get in within just hundreds of meters of the Dhora coastline before switching to closed-circuit rebreathers to approach the shoreline undetected. Due to the immense complexity of this task, the actual divers themselves would be predominantly sourced from Red Guard troops serving in the University of Qianxun Project 661 Lake Observatories, an institution renowned for possessing [url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=rmb/postid=60297287]some of the finest aquanauts in the world[/url].

Once at shore, instead of calling upon fleeing Dhora to swim, the divers would instead quickly fit any communists they could find with diving gear and organizing them into "teams". They're quickly taught the most basic steps for diving, the tools to operate, the use of buoyancy compensators during emergencies, hand signals, and anything else that will be necessary to save their lives. Then, after a quick test, the Dhora are ordered to walk into the shoreline where they would be escorted all the way back to the submersibles, and then back to the Astaniran vessels bound for Zurayq.

In the north, things would be more simplified, with SummitONE operatives and Balizids from the Emirate of Wali Zurayq being enlisted to patrol the northern fringes of the Dhora border for fleeing communists, whom they would flag down and intercept, then carefully escort along the treacherous, unbeaten path towards Zurayq. While SummitONE operatives would propose expanding this mission to involve border skirmishing to try and rescue even more communists, the Socintern Presidium would reject anything more as being far too incendiary for their liking.[/spoiler][/quote]

[b][u]Operation Misericordia - Continued[/u][/b]

The Dhora coast guard are far more trained in spotting surface vessels heading towards Dhora shores. The training they received as part of their mission to halt criminal gun smugglers from Sal-Baliz and GB made them well placed to detect surface vessels but this training wouldn't help them spot submersibles. When they saw the few swimmers attempting to make their way out of Dhornaper, they reacted instinctively and assumed they were criminals. When their orders for surrender were ignored, they opened fire. As far as they were aware, they were halting some sort of criminal enterprise, but what it could have been they did not know.

After the first few bodies were identified as wanted communists, questions swirled. Why were the communists attempting to escape by swimming from shore? Where did they expect to go? The Astanir ship build up, painfully obvious by how they covered just inside ULR's waters, raised suspicions that the Socialist International or some elements of it were attempting to rescue fleeing communists by sea, but as of yet, the threat wasn't taken seriously. After all, exile was just as acceptable as imprisonment to the government. Nevertheless, patrols across the shores were told to be on alert to catch communists attempting to escape by sea.

The northern border patrols similarly reported strange activity: an increased number of vehicles on the other side loitering and picking up passengers, a seeming patrol-like setup of civilian vehicles moving across in sweeps. The activity was unusual. But this went unnoticed as of now.

Back on the shore, the Qianxun divers and their submersibles arrived undetected. The coast guard not expecting anything other than small surface craft from criminal enterprises. Likewise, the passive sonar system surrounding Dhoranaper's waters would be of no use for such small vessels operating during regular civilian shipping. The subs sneaked right past the coast guard.

Once ashore, the Qianxun divers split up and moved individually for maximum concealment to avoid Dhora patrols. After each made it to their assigned rendezvous point, they moved on to their final jump off point. After giving them a whirlwind explanation and test on surviving the waters, they kitted them up and began to slowly extricate them to the shoreline. But not everyone made it to the rendezvous points.

A Qianxun diver had been spotted by a patrol jeep as it drove over the dead ground of a hill. His sudden dash into a culvert wasn't enough. The patrol stopped, ordered him out with his hands in the air. He popped his suicide pill and fell unconscious before the patrol grabbed his body. They immediately radiod in that they had an unresponsive captive in diving gear. It seemed to everyone that they had caught a particularly well-prepared fleeing communist. Their captive would be dead before they reached their processing centre.

A second diver had been spotted by an observation tower's night vision camera systems and was rapidly converged on by a patrol jeep. He was in cover when the jeep converted but the Dhora patrol's order to come out confirmed he was spotted. He popped his suicide pill likewise. A second well-equipped communist diver was captured, so they thought. But it was extremely unusual for two similarly equipped and unconscious captives to be found. Something was off.

The Dhora suspicions didn't stop the rest of the divers and their evacuees from making to shore and beginning the swim to the Astanir ships.

Dhornaper would take some time to unravel what had happened. The two corpses, silent witnesses, would say much about what happened and who was behind it.

[b]June 16, 2028: The Strømm Affair[/b]

Haakon Strømm walked casually along the streets of the Rosenmarkket capital of Tharkønn. He was headed to the National Peoples House, where the Council of 99 had begun to meet in late May following their relocation from their wartime HQ in Vespurias capital of Hyperion.

There had been word of a secessionist movement spreading through Rosenmarkke, with various groups having seemingly popped up overnight across the country demanding secession or re-union with Montfleur. 

Entering into the National Peoples House he made his way across the giant class foyer and into the main chamber of the hall, which had once held several hundred members of the legislature, but now only held the council of 99.

Gentlemen of the state, intoned Haakon as the 99 rose to greet him, Our country is at its most dire hour, he said as he moved to stand on the stage that faced the hall, walking behind the podium and leaning upon it. 

I shall now present you with a recent report I have brought with me, provided to me by the armed forces regarding these secessionist groups, he said, lifting a thick yellow-bound report.

12 of these groups exist in some capacity, he continued, opening the report, Membership, of course, gentlemen, varies, but is growingparticularly due to a figure by the name of Lambeau, continued Haakon. 

Now, the details are not as full as I wish, due to the lack of cohesion that has been established in forming a new SCSID, and I have reason to believe some of their people are conspiring with the Montfleurois government, whose king has openly called for re-unification, He said. 

Which is why I called you all here today, he stated, smiling as he looked up from the podium.

The council remained silent, one of the members coughed.

Haakon smiled once more and then spoke, Gentlemen, given these dangerous circumstances, I would like this council to vote on various measures along with an extension of the state of Emergency, Wuloosya still remains a threat even if we are at peace, in fact just yesterday the army arrested 15 people who were found to have committed espionage on behalf of the enemy,

One of the members of the council stood up, Josep Broz Østens, a law professor and the unofficial speaker for the council, Mr. Consul, I speak on behalf of this council when I say this, but the provisions which you sent us are highly unconstitutional, illegal, and paranoid, 

Haakon frowned, Name them, he pressed.

Suspension of the right of the press, mandatory military guard at protests and public gatherings, mandatory search and seizure of suspected foreign collaborators, sir with all due respect this is speedrunning the death of the state, replied Østens.

Haakon nodded thoughtfully and then said, Who let this man on this council? He looked at the council members.

Your predecessor sir, stated one of the councilmembers.

I see, and what is the constitutional prerogative for this council, what can I do as consul?

Dissolve and appoint new members, intoned Østens. 

Precisely, snapped Haakon. 

Thus, given the fact that this council has served its purpose, acting as a wartime government, I am dissolvng it, and will be appointing a new executive cabinet to ensure governmental continuity, he continued, as a group of military officers walked in, Gentlemen, thank you for your service,

He bowed as the council members stood confused, being moved out of the hall, some muttering amonst themselves.

Treason sir, said Østens calmly, This is treason, he continued as a guard escorted him out.

[b][u]The Rank of a Hundred Martyrs[/u][/b]

A few days later, the great reopening arrived. Hundreds of mullahs, clerics, and scholars arrived while the state news networks broadcasted the event over TV, radio, and the internet. President Fereydun Khan stayed aloof and detached from it. He wore a traditional langota, the Afghan choice of turban, and wrapped himself up in a shawl as he stayed seated at the front of a prepared stage outdoors in front of the renovated Khirqa Sharif Mosque. For now, he sat while Ayatollah Hossein spoke:

"I have something very important to say. We all know that the land, the water, and the air belong to Allah. So whose rules should govern Allah's country? The Elseyrians' rules? The Argosians' rules? The Kianzhous' rules?"

The gathering knew how to answer, they all rejected foreign interference. In unison, they called out

"No, Allah's rules!"

He continued.

"The Prophet said, 'If anyone is able to bring back the rules of the Quran in my name, what rank will that person then be given?'"

"The rank of one hundred martyrs!" Cried the mullahs.

The Ayatollah then announced that he wanted to give Fereydun Khan the highest title available in Islam, that of Amir al-Mu'minin, comparable to that of Pope in the Catholic church. The rules of Islam stipulated that only the Prophet himself or the ulema could grant it. Fereydun Khan had his ulema prepared. The last holder of it in Dhornaper had been the Shah, who inherited it from the time Nasrollah Shah was crowned it, over two hundred years ago.

"By making him the Amir, we are restoring our connection with the Quran, are we not? Do you too want the hundred martyrs? Do you too want the Quran restored? Will you make a pact with this Amir to achieve that? Or not?"

Again, Fereydun Khan sat there aloof while the mullahs called out in unison: "Yes, thats what we want!"

The Ayatollah concluded his speech with some words about country's leadership.

"Do you agree its time to restore the position of Amir al-Mu'minin?" He asked the audience.

Everyone answered in unison: "Yes!"

"Is His Excellency Fereydun Khan the general Amir of the Muslims?"

"Yes!"

At this point, Fereydun Khan came forward rather slowly to be congratulated by all the mullahs at the meeting, each of whom had to shake his hand, not just as a mere handshake, but as an oath to the Amir, a promise of support for as long as he lives.

After all present had swore their oath, Fereydun Khan went up to the microphone and began to speak.

"In the name of Allah..."

He was cut short. A loud whirring noise rapidly approached him. It was a makeshift kamikaze drone.

Seconds later, a loud blast rocked the platform. Fereydun Kham was thrown off the stage into seating area as his guards scrambled to shield him. He was bloodied and bruised but not badly injured. The drone had missed and hit the mosque behind him.
